newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London stall on election gloom.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London stall on election gloom.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were weaker on Thursday as political worries continued to weigh on the Tokyo stock market and Wall Street's lower close overnight dampened enthusiasm, dealers said.
In London, the Nikkei/Ise 50 index was down 1.61 points at 1,426.53 after the Nikkei 225 Average in Tokyo dropped for a fourth consecutive session to end just above 21,000 points.

"We really see no incentive to get into the London market as long as Tokyo remains weak. And until we know what political direction Japan is taking, there won't be too much business around," one dealer said.
The weekend's election proved inconclusive for markets as the business-friendly Liberal Democratic Party fell short of winning a majority in the lower house of parliament.
Traders had hoped for a win to allay nagging worries about taxation, business policies and a possible supplementary budget -- all factors deterring foreign investors.
Traders said shares in London were steady to weaker.
Sharp Corp dropped, after the electronics maker trimmed its parent profit forecast for the 1996/97 year to 74 billion yen from 77 billion previously.
